title: Building a UK neurodiversity support directory that checks itself
audience: Organisations that keep a public list or directory (members, suppliers, services) that goes out of date.

intent.primary: How can a public directory stay accurate without someone checking every listing by hand?
related: How do you stop sending people to organisations that have closed?

uniqueValue: A working, public example of self-checking records: nearly 900 listings re-checked every 1 to 3 days. Useful to anyone maintaining a list people rely on.

seo.title: Self-checking directory case study | Chris Demetriou
seo.description: How the Neuro Support Checker keeps nearly 900 UK support organisations up to date by re-checking every listing every 1 to 3 days.

role.summary: I designed and built the directory and its checking.

claims.text: The directory lists 897 UK organisations across 18 conditions (19 Oct 2026).
Listings are checked every 1 to 3 days, and daily if anything looks wrong; each shows when it was last checked.

body.text: By re-checking the listings on a schedule instead of by hand. The Neuro Support Checker lists 897 UK organisations across 18 conditions, and checks each one every 1 to 3 days, daily if anything looks wrong.

body.heading: What a visitor sees
body.text: Every listing shows when it was last checked, so a family can see straight away whether the information is current. The directory is free to use.
